messages:
ana: FYI — after we pushed NVIDIA driver 525.60 to a canary group of T4s in us-west1/us-west2, a few hosts lost their MIG partitions and pods are failing to schedule :grimacing:

mike: which hosts? any pattern (zone, kernel version, image)?

ana: affected: gpu-west1-03, gpu-west1-07, gpu-usw2-12. All T4s, same AMI, rolled over this morning between 07:10-07:25 UTC. Scheduler errors: "no matching GPU resources" even though node labels show capacity.

sre-bot: ALERT — MIG_PROFILE_DRIFT detected on gpu-west1-07 (incident INC-3842) — https://incidents.internal/INC-3842 :eyes:

chris: can you paste `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi mig -lgci` from one failing host? also `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `uname -r`. common culprit is kernel/driver ABI mismatch or module failing to initialize MIG subsystem.

ana: paste from gpu-west1-07:
```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: Tesla T4 (UUID: GPU-123abc45-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-123456abcdef)
$ nvidia-smi mig -lgci
No MIG devices found
$ uname -r
5.15.0-103-generic
$ dmesg | grep -i nvidia
[  23.456789] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[  23.456800] nvidia: Loading driver 525.60
[  23.457100] nvidia-modeset: Unregistered GPU 0000:03:00.0
[  23.457200] nvidia: MIG init failed: -22
```

mike: MIG init failed -22 usually points to either a driver build mismatch or a kernel module not matching the in-tree expectations. Any PCI/UUID drift reported? run `nvidia-smi -q | grep UUID` and `lspci -vnn | grep -i nvidia -A 2`.

ana: `nvidia-smi -q | grep UUID` returns the same UUID as before, but kubelet shows device plugin error: `device UUID mismatch` for the pods that bound to old UUIDs. Some nodes show ephemeral changes after driver reload.

chris: that matches past incidents where driver upgrade = brief kernel module reload -> device nodes re-created with different minor numbers and the plugin's cached mappings break. Two tracks: 1) try a graceful re-apply of MIG profiles on the host with `nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -cgi <cfg>` or `nvidia-smi mig -r && nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -c 1` depending on profile list; 2) if that doesn't work, reboot the node to force a clean module load (but coordinate with capacity).

ana: attempting reapply on gpu-west1-07 now:
```
sudo nvidia-smi mig -r
# purge old contexts
sudo nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -cgi 1g.5gb
Error: No MIG devices found
```

julia: hold on reboots — west1 capacity is low this afternoon. Please cordon+drain before rebooting. We don't want a cascade.

mike: agreed. also check kernel vs driver package: dpkg -l | grep nvidia or `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic`. If the module vermagic doesn't match the running kernel, module behavior is unstable.

ana: quick check on gpu-usw2-12 (still failing): `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` => `5.15.0-102 SMP mod_unload ` — oops that node is on 5.15.0-102 while others are 5.15.0-103. Looks like the image roll was partial.

chris: there you go — kernel mismatch. Driver userland 525.60 expects module built against 5.15.0-103. Options: upgrade kernel on that host (preferred) or rollback driver to one built for 5.15.0-102. Given we've rolled most nodes forward, schedule kernel update+reboot for gpu-usw2-12 during low traffic.

mike: long-term: we should add a post-driver-upgrade hook in our node image pipeline that runs the MIG reapply sequence and validates `nvidia-smi mig -lgci` before marking the node healthy. I'll open a PR for the hook and a small operator to reapply MIG profiles when device UUIDs change.

chris: will add the PR. Also check NCCL logs on any training jobs — driver reload can cause transient NCCL errors. We should run a quick sweep of recent pod logs for `NCCL WARN` messages.

ana: I've cordoned gpu-usw2-12 and scheduled a kernel patch+reboot for 02:00 UTC. Reapplied MIG successfully on west1-03 and west1-07 after controlled reboots; scheduler now schedules pods again. Still watching usw2-12 post-reboot.

julia: thanks. Action items: ana — remediate usw2-12 during the low window; chris — add post-upgrade MIG reapply hook PR; mike — add check to the driver rollout playbook to verify kernel vermagic before upgrade. We'll close after 24h no regressions. :thumbsup:

ana: noted — I'll report back in this thread after the reboot.
